D1 · Team

Add the team: quality engineer (owner), process engineer for reflow, line supervisor, and materials if paste is involved.

D2 · Problem description

Auto-filled
On the night shift of 15 Oct 2026, 47 CTRL-BRD-A boards from batch stg-B0003 on SMT line 2 showed solder bridging. 43 of the 47 were built after 02:00. Batches stg-B0001 and stg-B0002 were not affected.

D3 · Containment

Auto-filled
112 boards share the high peak reflow signature but passed AOI: hold WIP, quarantine finished goods, and notify the customer about boards already shipped. See the board list.

D4 · Root cause

Auto-filled
Occurrence
Peak reflow temperature rose to 258.6 °C (spec 245–255 °C) from 02:00, causing excess solder spreading. 44 of 47 bridged boards were above the upper limit. Confidence 98.9%.
Escape
Why didn't the line catch the reflow drift earlier? Confirm whether a peak-temperature alarm exists on the oven.
Contributing: stencil thickness above spec on 11 boards (72.5%). See full analysis

D5 · Corrective action

Auto-filled
  • Restore the approved reflow profile; check the peak-zone setpoint and thermocouple.
  • Use a thinner foil or step-down stencil; verify the stencil ID against the job.

D6 · Verification

Needs input
Record the verification run: profile measurement after the fix and bridging rate over the next [N] panels.

D7 · Prevention

Auto-filled
Add a peak reflow upper-limit alarm on line 2. This case was added to the Failure Library so the same pattern is flagged automatically next time.
